name: MonarchPeriodSelector
title: PeriodSelector
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow with SegmentedButton (or MonarchSelect), and androidx.compose.material3.DateRangePicker in a DatePickerDialog for custom dates
summary: Picks the period a dashboard or a report covers, from presets such as Last 7 days and This quarter or custom dates in the Material 3 date range picker.
whenToUse: Above a dashboard, a chart or a report whose numbers depend on a period, when people mostly want common periods and sometimes exact dates.
whenNotToUse: For a date range a form needs (a booking, a leave request), use the Material 3 DateRangePicker on its own (date-range-picker). For one date, use the DatePicker.
api: @Composable fun MonarchPeriodSelector(value: MonarchPeriodValue, onValueChange: (MonarchPeriodValue) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, presets: List<MonarchPeriodPreset> = MonarchPeriodSelectorDefaults.Presets, variant: MonarchPeriodSelectorVariant = MonarchPeriodSelectorVariant.Segmented, enabled: Boolean = true, showRange: Boolean = false, today: Long? = null, firstDayOfWeek: Int? = null, minDate: Long? = null, maxDate: Long? = null, maxDays: Int? = null, locale: Locale? = null, timeZone: String? = null, labels: MonarchPeriodSelectorLabels = MonarchPeriodSelectorLabels())
data class MonarchPeriodValue(val preset: MonarchPeriodPreset, val range: MonarchPeriodRange? = null)
data class MonarchPeriodRange(val startMillis: Long, val endMillis: Long)

enum class MonarchPeriodPreset { Today, Yesterday, Last7Days, Last14Days, Last30Days, Last90Days, Last180Days, Last365Days, ThisWeek, ThisMonth, LastMonth, ThisQuarter, LastQuarter, ThisYear, Custom }

object MonarchPeriodSelectorDefaults { val Presets: List<MonarchPeriodPreset>; fun today(nowMillis: Long = System.currentTimeMillis(), timeZone: String? = null): Long; fun firstDayOfWeek(locale: Locale): Int; fun resolve(value: MonarchPeriodValue, today: Long, firstDayOfWeek: Int = Calendar.MONDAY): MonarchPeriodRange? }

class MonarchPeriodSelectorLabels(label: String? = null, preset: ((MonarchPeriodPreset) -> String)? = null, customRange: String? = null, chooseDates: String? = null, confirm: String? = null, cancel: String? = null, tooLong: ((maxDays: Int) -> String)? = null)

options.name: value
options.description: The period shown: a preset, and for Custom the picked days.

options.name: onValueChange
options.description: Called when a preset is chosen or custom dates are saved. Choosing Custom reports the dates shown until then and opens the picker. Get the days of any period with MonarchPeriodSelectorDefaults.resolve.

options.name: presets
options.description: The presets offered, in order, as on the web.

options.name: variant
options.description: Segments that scroll sideways when they do not fit, or a MonarchSelect field with a menu, better for many presets on a phone.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the period can be changed.

options.name: showRange
options.description: Shows the days a preset covers under the control, such as "Nov 9 – 15, 2026".

options.name: today
options.description: Today as UTC midnight. null uses the device's date in timeZone. Pass it for a workspace time zone or a fixed date.

options.name: firstDayOfWeek
options.description: The first day of This week, a java.util.Calendar day constant. null uses the locale's.

options.name: minDate
options.description: The earliest day custom dates may start, UTC midnight.

options.name: maxDate
options.description: The latest day custom dates may end, UTC midnight. null is today.

options.name: maxDays
options.description: The longest custom range in days. A longer range shows "Choose 30 days or fewer" and Save stays off.

options.name: locale
options.description: The locale of the written dates and of the week. null uses the configuration's.

options.name: timeZone
options.description: The zone whose calendar day is today when today is null. An IANA id such as Europe/Berlin; null, or an id the device does not know, is the device's zone.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string: the name, each preset, the custom button, Save, Cancel and the too-long message.

states.name: preset
states.description: The chosen segment is selected (filled with a check mark); with showRange its days are written under the row.

states.name: custom, no dates
states.description: A button "Choose dates" under the presets opens the date range picker.

states.name: custom with dates
states.description: The button shows the dates, such as "Oct 3 – Nov 15, 2026", and opens the picker on them.

states.name: picking
states.description: The Material 3 DateRangePicker in a dialog. Days before minDate and after maxDate cannot be picked. Save is off until a first day is picked and while the range is longer than maxDays; one picked day saves a one-day range.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Every segment, the select field and the custom button are disabled; the dates use the disabled text color.

appearance: The Material 3 segmented buttons in the Monarch theme: the outline border, the selected segment filled with the secondary container color and a check mark. The dates under the row use the caption style in the muted text role, the disabled role when disabled. The too-long message uses the danger strong role. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from MonarchTheme.
platformNotes: The web has the presets as a segmented control or a Select and the DateRangePicker field inline under them. On Android the custom dates are picked in the Material 3 DateRangePicker dialog, opened as soon as Custom is chosen and again from a button that shows the dates. The web's size prop (sm, md) is not offered: Material 3 segmented buttons have one height with a 48dp target. Dates are UTC midnight epoch milliseconds as in the Material 3 pickers, not ISO strings. The web calls onValueChange with the value and the resolved range; on Android onValueChange takes the value and MonarchPeriodSelectorDefaults.resolve gives the range. The web's dateRangeMessages are the Material 3 picker's own strings, translated by the system; Save, Cancel and the too-long message are in labels. iOS has not built this component yet.
accessibility: Each preset is a Material 3 segmented button, read as a radio button with its selected state; the row is named "Period" for TalkBack.
Every segment, the custom dates button and the select field have a 48dp touch target.
The custom dates button is read as "Custom period" and its dates, or "Choose dates".
A range longer than maxDays is said in words above the calendar, in a polite live region, and Save is disabled.
The segment row scrolls sideways instead of cutting labels at font scale 2.0, and the dates under it wrap.
In right to left the first preset is at the right.
edgeCases: Rolling periods count today: Last 7 days on 15 November is 9 to 15 November.
This week starts on the locale's first day; pass firstDayOfWeek for a workspace setting.
Last month and last quarter are whole months, so Last month on 31 March is 1 to 28 February.
Choosing Custom keeps the dates shown until then, so the picker opens on them; Cancel keeps them.
A custom value without a range resolves to null; the app shows nothing until dates are saved.
today is the device's date at composition; pass today when the period must follow a workspace time zone.

examples.title: Every preset in a select field, custom up to a year
examples.code:
MonarchPeriodSelector(
    value = period,
    onValueChange = { period = it },
    presets = MonarchPeriodPreset.entries,
    variant = MonarchPeriodSelectorVariant.Select,
    maxDays = 366,
)
